name: toolbar
title: Toolbar
description: A row of commands that is one Tab stop (Base UI Toolbar): item cells on shared seams, groups on a 2px keyline, toggles that flood, an exclusive group whose ink band stretches, menus docked to the frame, a text input cell; horizontal or vertical.
whenToUse: Use it for a row of commands that is one Tab stop and folds secondary controls into a More menu when narrow. For a few buttons that each take a Tab stop use Button group.

parts.name: Toolbar
parts.description: A row of commands that is ONE Tab stop (Base UI Toolbar): arrow keys move between items and wrap at the ends (`loopFocus`, default true). Home and End are left to the focused item, as Base UI 1.9 does (the APG lists them as optional for toolbars), so a text input cell keeps them. Every item is a cell of one frame. items share 1px seams · a group meets its neighbours on a 2px keyline · a spacer is an empty cell - Give it `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`): a toolbar is a named landmark of controls. - Groups (ToolbarGroup, ToolbarToggleGroup) are units: their outer edges are control weight (2px), so a group reads as one control inside the row without a gap (C1). ToolbarSeparator draws the same 2px keyline between ungrouped items and is announced as a separator. - Disabled items stay focusable (Base UI's default), so a keyboard user still finds them and hears why. - Narrow: a horizontal toolbar scrolls inside its frame and fades the edge where items are hidden (scroll edges); focus scrolls the focused item into view. With overflow="menu" the items that don't fit move into a "More" menu instead (the primary item and text inputs never move), in either orientation. Items are found by their data-slot, so an item wrapped in a Tooltip, or rendered by a component of yours, moves like any other; a folded item stays mounted (hidden), so its state stays. - Arrow keys follow the DOM `dir` (an RTL subtree reverses Left/Right), not only a DirectionProvider.

props.name: layout
props.description: control (default): its own 2px frame and the cut. cell: a row of an enclosing frame (a panel's top cell, a shell header).

props.name: overflow
props.description: What a toolbar does when its items don't fit. scroll (default): it scrolls inside its frame and fades the hidden edge. menu: items that don't fit leave, last first, and a "More" item takes their place; its menu holds them as rows (a button is an item, a toggle a checkbox item, an exclusive group radio items, a menu a submenu), with their state. A ToolbarGroup gives up its items one at a time (they appear under its label); `keepTogether` makes it leave whole. Horizontal, the toolbar then spans its line; vertical (a palette), it takes the height its container gives it and More sits at its foot, opening to the side.

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the overflow item ("More"); its menu says how many items it holds.

props.name: overflowTrigger
props.description: icon (default): the overflow item is a square ⋯ cell named by overflowLabel. label: it shows overflowLabel as text with a caret, for a row whose items may all move into it.

parts.name: ToolbarButton
parts.description: A command cell (Base UI Toolbar.Button). Contents travel 1px on press (Key); the cell never floods: an action holds no state.

props.name: affix
props.description: A trailing cell inside the item: a count or a shortcut (mono when it is a <kbd> or a code).

props.name: icon
props.description: Square cell for a glyph-only item. Give it aria-label; pair with a Tooltip for sighted users.

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: The item's name as a row of the overflow menu, when its text is not enough (a glyph item uses aria-label).

props.name: primary
props.description: The one primary action of the row: the cobalt cell (commit signal). At most one per toolbar. It never moves into the overflow menu.

props.name: signal
props.description: Button's signal: pending runs a segment along the bottom keyline (busy, still focusable); done inserts a ✓ cell; failed a ! cell at the start.

parts.name: ToolbarGroup
parts.description: Items that belong together, drawn as one control (2px outer edges). With overflow="menu" its items move into More one at a time, from the end, and appear there under the group's label; `keepTogether` moves the group only as a whole (an alignment set, a pair that means nothing apart).

parts.name: ToolbarInput
parts.description: A text input cell (Base UI Toolbar.Input). Arrow keys move the caret; they leave the input for the neighbouring item only at the text's ends. Its edge is the cell's (`kl-edge`, a 2px band on the keylines), as the table search's is. `label` names it for assistive technology; `glyph` leads it.

props.name: cellClassName
props.description: Classes for the cell (the label element that holds the glyph and the input). `className`, `style` and `render` are the input's (Base UI Toolbar.Input), as for every part.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the input for assistive technology.

parts.name: ToolbarLink
parts.description: A link cell (Base UI Toolbar.Link): navigation, not a command. Underlined like a quiet button.

parts.name: ToolbarMenuContent
parts.description: The menu of a ToolbarMenuTrigger. Menu's surface and rows (MenuItem, MenuCheckboxItem, MenuRadioItem, submenus from ./menu); its top border lies on the toolbar's bottom keyline at the toolbar's weight (2px framed, 1px as a cell), so trigger and menu read as one shape. No cut. Carries the configuration of the place it is written (cut, theme, density, motion, dir) into the portal.

parts.name: ToolbarMenuTrigger
parts.description: A menu title in the row: Base UI Menu.Trigger rendered as a toolbar item, with a caret cell. Open, it is the inverse cell; its menu docks to the toolbar's keyline under it (ToolbarMenuContent). The toolbar's own Menu root is Base UI's: <ToolbarMenu><ToolbarMenuTrigger>…</ToolbarMenuTrigger><ToolbarMenuContent>…

props.name: affix
props.description: A trailing cell before the caret: a count ("7/7") or a shortcut.

props.name: primary
props.description: The row's one commit action opens a menu (Assign ▾): the cobalt cell. It never moves into the overflow menu.

parts.name: ToolbarSeparator
parts.description: A 2px keyline between items, announced as a separator. Not needed between groups (they draw their own).

parts.name: ToolbarSpacer
parts.description: An empty cell that takes the free space, pushing what follows to the end. Not focusable, not announced.

parts.name: ToolbarToggle
parts.description: A toggle cell: Base UI Toggle rendered as a toolbar item, so it joins the row's arrow-key order. On its own or in a multiple ToolbarToggleGroup it is independent state: it floods yellow from the press point and carries a lamp (as ToggleGroup's cells do). In an exclusive group (multiple={false}) it is a choice among options: no lamp, and the group's ink band stretches to it (as Segmented's does).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: The toggle's name as a checkbox row of the overflow menu, when its text is not enough.

parts.name: ToolbarToggleGroup
parts.description: Toggles that belong together (Base UI ToggleGroup inside the toolbar's focus order). `multiple` (default true): independent toggles, each floods. multiple={false}: an exclusive choice (alignment, view), the ink band stretches between cells, leading edge first, zero bounce.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: (value: string[], eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void
